costGuide.title: Mercedes-Benz OM651.980 Engine Replacement Cost (UK)
costGuide.labourLine: Fitting an OM651 engine typically takes 8-12 hours at £65-£85/hr (independent) - confirm exact labour when comparing quotes.
paragraphs: What genuinely moves the price for this specific high-output engine is the condition of the turbocharger(s), intercooler piping, and whether the notorious timing chain tensioner (subject to TSB LI80.20-P-050001) has been proactively replaced. Because the OM651.980 operates at higher thermal loads, recon specialists will typically strip the top end to replace all critical seals and verify the chain tensioner upgrade as standard. failures.title: Mercedes-Benz OM651.980 Engine Problems - What Actually Fails

items.title: Timing Chain Tensioner Wear (TSB LI80.20-P-050001)
items.whatHappens: The early OM651 timing chain tensioner can fail, leading to chain slack, a distinct metallic rattle on cold starts, and potentially catastrophic valve-to-piston contact if the chain jumps a tooth.
items.repairVsReplace: Mercedes issued an updated tensioner design to resolve this. If caught early, replacing the tensioner and chain is cost-effective. If valve damage has already occurred, a full reconditioned OM651 unit is required.

items.title: Injector Seal Weeping ("Black Death")
items.whatHappens: The copper washer seals at the base of the injectors degrade, allowing high-pressure combustion gases to escape. This creates a black, crusty carbon buildup around the injector heads, leading to a distinct tapping noise, rough idling, and a strong smell of exhaust in the cabin.
items.repairVsReplace: This is a routine maintenance item, not a terminal failure. Replacing the seals and cleaning the cylinder head is inexpensive and should be done preventatively.

items.title: Turbocharger and Intercooler Stress
items.whatHappens: Due to the higher 204 hp output, the turbocharger(s) and intercooler system endure greater thermal and mechanical stress. Actuator wear or intercooler pipe splits can lead to boost leaks, limp mode, and increased soot loading in the DPF.
items.repairVsReplace: Intercooler pipe replacement is a straightforward and cost-effective repair. If the turbocharger internals have suffered damage from prolonged boost leaks or oil starvation, a full turbo rebuild or replacement is necessary.

failures.goodYearsLine: Post-2015 units with the updated timing chain tensioner and revised ECU mapping show significantly fewer catastrophic chain failures, making them the most desirable examples of this high-output engine family .

variants.title: How to Confirm You Have the Mercedes-Benz OM651.980
variants.intro: ═══════════════════════════════════════ The engine code is stamped on the right-hand side of the cylinder block, just above the oil filter housing. It will also be listed on your V5C logbook under "Engine Capacity" or visible via a VIN decode. The OM651.980 is the specific 204 hp (150 kW) high-output variant of the OM651 family. It is sometimes confused with the lower-output OM651.911/912 (136-170 hp), the standard OM651.924/925 (136 hp), or the commercial OM651.955-958 variants. Fitting the wrong revision or assuming interchangeability matters significantly: the OM651.980 features specific high-output internals, distinct turbo plumbing, intercooler piping, and ECU mapping that will not function correctly if swapped with a lower-output OM651 variant without extensive and costly modification.

buyingGuide.title: Buying a Replacement OM651.980 Engine - What to Choose

options.label: Used
options.body: A used OM651.980 engine makes sense only if it comes with verifiable service history and documented proof that the updated timing chain tensioner is installed, alongside a clean turbo health check. Given the catastrophic risk of chain failure in high-output applications, buying a used unit with unknown history is a significant financial risk.

options.label: Reconditioned
options.body: A proper reconditioned OM651 engine is the sweet spot for most buyers. A reputable rebuild will proactively address the common failure points by installing the updated timing chain tensioner, fitting new injector seals, and refreshing the turbo and intercooler components, giving the engine a fresh lease on life.

options.label: Rebuilt
options.body: A full OM651 engine rebuild is justified for high-mileage Sprinter hosts or enthusiast R172 SLK/SLC owners where maximum longevity and originality are required. An upgraded rebuild should include line-boring the block, new pistons/rings, and a balanced crankshaft.

buyingGuide.supplyFitLine: Sourcing and fitting through our vetted network ensures your OM651 engine is installed by specialists familiar with high-output Mercedes CDI systems, backed by a nationwide warranty.
buyingGuide.vehicleValueNote: Because the OM651.980 is typically found in R172, W212, X204, W166, and 906 vehicles valued between £8,000 and £25,000+, a full replacement is generally financially viable and comfortably within the host vehicle's value . Replacement cost rarely exceeds the scrap threshold for these chassis, making a reconditioned unit a highly sensible investment.

items.question: What is the most common failure on the OM651.980 engine?
items.answer: The most documented issues are timing chain tensioner wear (addressed under TSB LI80.20-P-050001), injector seal weeping ("Black Death"), and turbocharger or intercooler stress.
